messages:
alex: Anyone else seeing a surge of Pending tiny-gang pods in apse1? started at ~13:10 UTC, looks like warmpool slots aren't being claimed.
maria: yep noticed it at 13:12. many tiny-gang pods stuck Pending, warmpool nodes show slots reserved but not allocated.
jun: digging into scheduler logs, seeing repeated lease commit timeouts from the warmnode coalescer:
```
E0503 13:12:23 coalescer.go:412] commit lease timeout warmnode=w-n-87 err=kvcache.stale
E0503 13:12:24 coalescer.go:412] commit lease timeout warmnode=w-n-88
```
alex: could this be the short commit timeout we rolled to 30s on the canary?
ops-jen: I can cordon w-n-87 and restart the coalescer agent, low traffic right now. that usually clears stale leases. any objections?
maria: fine from product side, user impact is minimal. will notify support if any customer-facing jobs are blocked. :thumbsup:
jun: note: PR #1209 makes stale leases reclaimable after 45s, but i'd rather not deploy scheduler logic mid-incident. restart seems safer.
ops-jen: executing drain+restart:
```
$ kubectl cordon w-n-87
node/w-n-87 cordoned
$ kubectl drain w-n-87 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
evicting pod tiny-gang-x1y2z
```
ops-jen: restarted coalescer service, watching metrics.
sre-bot: Incident INC-20230503-43 opened. rule/pending_gang_rate triggered. severity: low.
maria: warmnode freed 6 slots within 90s after restart; pending tiny-gang count dropping. looks resolved for now.
jun: will file a postmortem and bisect the lease commit timeout change. suspect interaction between kvcache TTL and attach churn.
alex: follow-ups: add coalesce.commit.latency metric, alert if p95 > 25s; add runbook step to restart coalescer agent if >5 pending-gangs for >5m.
ops-jen: noted, will update runbook and attach commands + kubectl output.
alex: thanks team. keeping thread until postmortem published.
